universities.name: Politecnico di Milano
universities.description: Italy's largest technical university, focused on engineering, architecture, and design. Based in Milan with strong international placement and one of the most-recognised Italian institutions for graduate study in technical fields.

universities.name: Bocconi University
universities.description: A private Italian university in Milan specialising in economics, management, finance, and law, with strong international placement in business and finance.

universities.name: Delft University of Technology
universities.description: The largest and oldest Dutch technological university, with research strengths across engineering, computer science, and applied sciences.

universities.name: Eindhoven University of Technology
universities.description: A research university in the Brainport Eindhoven region, specialising in engineering and technology with close partnerships with the Dutch high-tech industry.

universities.name: Erasmus University Rotterdam
universities.description: A Dutch research university with international reputation in economics, business, social sciences, and health.

universities.name: Technical University of Munich
universities.description: A leading German research university covering engineering, natural sciences, life sciences, medicine, and management.

universities.name: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology
universities.description: A German public research university in Baden-Württemberg combining a traditional technical university with a national research centre, with strengths in engineering, natural sciences, and computing.

universities.name: University of Mannheim
universities.description: A German public research university in southwestern Germany, particularly well-known for economics, business, and the social sciences.

universities.name: London School of Economics and Political Science
universities.description: A world-leading social science university in central London, focused on economics, politics, law, and international relations.

universities.name: London Business School
universities.description: A specialist postgraduate business school of the University of London, consistently ranked among the world's top business schools.

universities.name: Imperial College London
universities.description: A research university in central London focused on science, engineering, medicine, and business.

universities.name: IE University
universities.description: A private Spanish university with campuses in Madrid and Segovia, internationally recognised for its business school and graduate programmes. Highly diverse student body (160+ nationalities) with English-taught masters across management, finance, analytics, law, and the humanities.

universities.name: Esade
universities.description: A private Spanish business and law school based in Barcelona, part of Ramon Llull University. Consistently ranked among the world's top business schools for its Master in Management, Master in Finance, and MBA programmes.

universities.name: Universidad Carlos III de Madrid
universities.description: A young public Spanish research university based in Madrid (Getafe, Leganés, Colmenarejo), known for strengths in economics, business, engineering, and law, with a notable share of English-taught masters.

universities.name: IESE Business School
universities.description: The graduate business school of the University of Navarra, based in Barcelona with additional campuses in Madrid, Munich, New York, and São Paulo. Consistently ranked among the world's top business schools for its MBA, Executive MBA, and Master in Management.

universities.name: NOVA School of Business and Economics
universities.description: The business and economics school of NOVA University Lisbon, based on a modern campus in Carcavelos near Lisbon. The parent NOVA University Lisbon is ranked in the QS World University Rankings 2025; NOVA SBE is consistently ranked among Europe's top business schools for finance, management, and economics.

universities.name: HEC Paris
universities.description: A leading French grande école and graduate business school based on the Jouy-en-Josas campus south of Paris, consistently ranked among the world's top schools for its Master in Management and other specialised masters, with strong placement in consulting, finance, and tech across Europe.

universities.name: Institut Polytechnique de Paris
universities.description: A public institute of science and technology grouping École Polytechnique with ENSTA, ENSAE, Télécom Paris, and Télécom SudParis on the Paris-Saclay plateau. Known for elite engineering, mathematics, computer science, and quantitative finance programmes, with a growing portfolio of English-taught masters.

universities.name: Sciences Po
universities.description: A French research university in central Paris specialising in the social sciences — political science, international affairs, public policy, economics, sociology, and law — with seven graduate schools and a strong international student body.

universities.name: ESSEC Business School
universities.description: A French grande école based north-west of Paris with additional campuses in Singapore and Rabat, particularly strong in management, finance, and luxury brand management, and consistently ranked among the top European business schools.

universities.name: ESCP Business School
universities.description: The world's oldest business school, founded in Paris in 1819, with six European campuses (Paris, London, Berlin, Madrid, Turin, Warsaw) and a flagship multi-campus Master in Management ranked among the very best in the world.

universities.name: ETH Zurich
universities.description: A Swiss federal institute of technology in Zurich, ETH is one of the world's leading STEM-focused research universities, with 22 affiliated Nobel laureates and broad strengths across engineering, computer science, natural sciences, and architecture.

universities.name: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne
universities.description: A Swiss federal institute of technology in Lausanne, EPFL is one of Europe's most international technical universities, with strong programmes across computer science, engineering, life sciences, and architecture.

universities.name: University of St. Gallen
universities.description: A Swiss public university specialising in business administration, economics, law, international affairs, and computer science. HSG is consistently ranked among Europe's leading business schools and is known for strong placement into consulting, banking, and corporate management.

universities.name: TU Wien
universities.description: Austria's largest technical research university, founded in 1815 and based in Vienna, with strengths in computer science, data science, engineering, mathematics, and architecture.

universities.name: WU Vienna University of Economics and Business
universities.description: Austria's leading public university for business and economics, based in Vienna. Triple-accredited (AACSB, EQUIS, AMBA) with a strongly international student body and an extensive portfolio of English-taught master's programmes.

universities.name: KTH Royal Institute of Technology
universities.description: Sweden's largest technical university, with research and teaching strengths across engineering and technology. Member of the CESAER and UNITE! European university networks, with consistently top-25 QS subject placements in mechanical, materials, and electrical engineering.

universities.name: Lund University
universities.description: One of Northern Europe's oldest and most comprehensive research universities, with eight faculties spanning engineering, sciences, economics, social sciences, law, and the humanities. Anchors major research infrastructures including MAX IV and the European Spallation Source.

universities.name: Stockholm School of Economics
universities.description: A small, selective private business school in central Stockholm focused on economics, finance, accounting, and management. Triple-crown-adjacent through EQUIS accreditation and CEMS membership, with consistent top-30 Financial Times rankings for its master's programmes.

universities.name: Technical University of Denmark
universities.description: A leading European engineering university just north of Copenhagen, member of the EuroTech Universities Alliance alongside EPFL and TU Munich. Strong research output across engineering, applied sciences, and biotechnology.

universities.name: Copenhagen Business School
universities.description: One of the largest business schools in Northern Europe, holding triple-crown accreditation (EQUIS, AMBA, AACSB). Programmes span economics, business administration, and interdisciplinary tracks combining business with humanities, social sciences, and technology.

universities.name: Aalto University
universities.description: Finnish research university created in 2010 by merging the Helsinki University of Technology, Helsinki School of Economics, and University of Art and Design Helsinki. Distinctive cross-disciplinary structure across engineering, business, and design — globally top-ranked for art & design.

universities.name: University of Oxford
universities.description: A collegiate research university and the oldest university in the English-speaking world, with teaching dating back to 1096. Comprises 43 colleges and four academic divisions across the city of Oxford, with global research strengths spanning humanities, social sciences, mathematical and physical sciences, and medicine.

universities.name: University of Cambridge
universities.description: A collegiate research university and the world's third-oldest university in continuous operation, founded in 1209 by scholars who departed Oxford. Comprises 31 self-governing colleges and more than 150 academic departments, with affiliated academics having won 126 Nobel Prizes.

universities.name: University College London
universities.description: A large public research university and a member of the Russell Group, founded in 1826 as the first university institution established in London. Operates across eleven faculties from its main Bloomsbury campus, with broad strength across the sciences, engineering, humanities, and social sciences.

universities.name: University of Edinburgh
universities.description: A public research university and one of Scotland's ancient universities, founded by royal charter in 1582. The largest university in Scotland, with five main campuses across the city and particular strengths in informatics, data science, life sciences, and the social sciences.

universities.name: Trinity College Dublin
universities.description: The sole constituent college of the University of Dublin and Ireland's oldest university, established by royal charter in 1592. A research-led university with three faculties and 25 schools, consistently the highest-ranked university in Ireland.

universities.name: KU Leuven
universities.description: The largest university in Belgium and the oldest university in the Low Countries, founded in 1425. A leading European research university with broad disciplinary coverage; many graduate programmes are taught in English despite Dutch being the primary language of instruction.

universities.name: Sapienza Università di Roma
universities.description: One of Europe's largest and oldest universities, founded in 1303 by Pope Boniface VIII. A comprehensive public research university in central Rome with broad strengths across the humanities, social sciences, engineering, computer science, and the natural sciences. Hosts a growing portfolio of English-taught master's programmes for international students.

universities.name: University of Bologna
universities.description: The oldest university in continuous operation in the Western world, founded in 1088. A comprehensive public research university with its main campus in Bologna and additional campuses in Cesena, Forlì, Ravenna, and Rimini. Strong international presence with a wide range of English-taught second-cycle (master's) degree programmes.

universities.name: University of Warwick
universities.description: A leading UK research university near Coventry, founded in 1965. Particularly recognised for Warwick Business School (WBS), economics, mathematics, and computer science. Strong industry links and consistently ranked in the UK top 10 and the world top 100.

universities.name: University of Manchester
universities.description: A major Russell Group research university in northern England, with origins going back to 1824. Comprehensive academic portfolio across engineering, life sciences, business (Alliance Manchester Business School), social sciences, and the humanities, with one of the largest postgraduate communities in the UK.

universities.name: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich
universities.description: A leading German public research university in Munich, founded in 1472, consistently ranked among the top universities in continental Europe. Particularly strong in economics, the humanities, life sciences, physics, and medicine, with a growing offer of English-taught master's programmes.

universities.name: RWTH Aachen University
universities.description: Germany's largest technical university and a member of the IDEA League and TU9 alliance of leading German technical universities. Located in Aachen close to the Belgian and Dutch borders, with a strong industry-oriented research profile in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, and materials science.

universities.name: University of Amsterdam
universities.description: The largest comprehensive research university in the Netherlands, located in Amsterdam, with origins as the Athenaeum Illustre in 1632. Wide-ranging academic profile covering economics and business, social and behavioural sciences, humanities, law, science, and medicine, with more than 150 English-taught master's programmes.

universities.name: Universitat Pompeu Fabra
universities.description: A young public research university in Barcelona, founded in 1990 and named after Catalan philologist Pompeu Fabra. Internationally recognised for economics, finance, political and social sciences, and communication, and closely associated with the Barcelona School of Economics (BSE) for graduate programmes.

universities.name: Norwegian University of Science and Technology
universities.description: Norway's largest university and its primary institution for engineering and the natural sciences, with strong programmes across technology, architecture, medicine, social sciences, and the humanities. As a Norwegian public university, NTNU charges no tuition to students from the EU/EEA and Switzerland; non-EEA students pay tuition fees set by the institution.

universities.name: University of Oslo
universities.description: Norway's oldest and most comprehensive research university, with broad strengths across natural sciences, social sciences, humanities, law, and medicine. As a Norwegian public university, UiO charges no tuition to students from the EU/EEA and Switzerland; non-EEA students pay tuition fees from the 2023/2024 academic year onward.

universities.name: BI Norwegian Business School
universities.description: Norway's largest business school and one of Europe's leading institutions for management education, with a triple-accredited (EQUIS, AACSB, AMBA) portfolio of English-taught master's programmes in finance, business analytics, and strategic management. Unlike Norwegian public universities, BI charges tuition to all students regardless of nationality.

universities.name: Charles University
universities.description: Founded in 1348, Charles University is one of the oldest universities in the world and the largest and most prestigious in the Czech Republic, with strengths across the humanities, social sciences, law, medicine, and the natural sciences. Czech-taught programmes are tuition-free for all nationalities at public universities; English-taught programmes charge tuition.

universities.name: Czech Technical University in Prague
universities.description: Founded in 1707, CTU is one of the oldest technical universities in Europe and the leading Czech institution for engineering, computer science, and architecture, with a broad portfolio of English-taught master's programmes including the well-known Open Informatics track at the Faculty of Electrical Engineering.

universities.name: University of Warsaw
universities.description: Poland's leading research university and the country's only institution ranked among the top 300 globally, with established strengths in economics, the social sciences, mathematics, and the humanities, and a growing portfolio of English-taught master's programmes in the Faculty of Economic Sciences.

universities.name: University of Tartu
universities.description: Estonia's national university and the leading research institution in the Baltic region, founded in 1632 by King Gustav II Adolf of Sweden. Strengths include computer science, life sciences, semiotics, and the social sciences, with around 70 master's programmes available, many taught in English.

universities.name: Royal College of Art
universities.description: A wholly postgraduate art and design university in London, ranked the world's number one university for art and design by QS for twelve consecutive years (2014–2026). Programmes span design, architecture, communication, fine art, and humanities, with strong industry collaboration across the Battersea, Kensington, and White City campuses.

universities.name: Goldsmiths, University of London
universities.description: A constituent college of the University of London, internationally recognised for the arts, design, media, and social sciences. Based in New Cross, south-east London, with a creative-practice ethos and ranked among the top universities globally for art and design and communication and media studies.

universities.name: Hertie School
universities.description: Germany's leading private graduate school of governance and public policy, based in central Berlin. Offers English-taught masters and PhD programmes combining political science, economics, law, and data science to train future policymakers and public-sector leaders.

universities.name: Geneva Graduate Institute
universities.description: A graduate-level research institute in Geneva (IHEID), founded in 1927 as the world's first graduate school dedicated solely to international affairs. Specialises in international relations, development studies, international law, and global governance, with deep links to the Geneva-based UN system and international organisations.

universities.name: King's College London
universities.description: A research-intensive Russell Group university and a constituent college of the University of London, founded in 1829. Strong global standing in the humanities, social sciences, law, medicine, and war studies, with five central London campuses on or near the Strand.
